info.label: Tool Dissectional
info.desc: "Lateralus" is the third studio album by the American rock band Tool. It was released on May 15, 2001, through Volcano Entertainment. Recording took place at Cello Studios in Hollywood and at The Hook, Big Empty Space, and The Lodge in North Hollywood between October 2000 and January 2001. David Bottrill, who had also produced the band's previous releases "Ænima" and "Salival", co-produced the album with the band. "Lateralus" remains the last Tool album produced by Bottrill. The album debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 chart, selling over 555,200 copies in its first week. It was certified triple .

podcast.body: Produced by David Botrell, this album saw significant internal conflict during its recording, particularly concerning Maynard's lyrics which were challenging for Adam Jones to hear. The band experienced legal problems between *Anima* and *Lateralus*, firing their manager and issues with the record company, which strained their relationship and nearly led to the band's end during the recording of *Lateralus*. "It was almost the end of the tool at that point."

podcast.body: Released on May 15, 2001, just six months after *Salival*, this album came out on the Volcano label, specifically through Dissectional, Tool's co-owned sub-label. Despite emerging after four prolonged years of legal disputes, the album demonstrated the strength of Tool's dedicated fanbase by selling over half a million copies in its first seven days. The band toured extensively in support of *Lateralus* throughout 2001 and 2002. "Lateralus was released on May 15th of 2000, just six months after Salival."

podcast.body: This album is considered an absolute masterpiece, one of the best in rock history, and one of the most complex ever made, comparable to the greatest works created. It uniquely combines a narrative theme with a structural-rhythmic theme, the latter being rare in music history, and is entirely based on the complex mathematical concepts of the Golden Ratio and the Fibonacci sequence. "obra absolutamente maestra, yo creo que con muchísima diferencia uno de los mejores discos a la historia del rock y uno de los discos más complejos jamás hechos."

podcast.body: This album is widely recognized as a pivotal work in rock history, released with considerable anticipation following the critical and commercial success of its predecessor. The band dedicated years to its development, creating extensive demos at home before a more concentrated three-month studio recording period. Produced by Tool themselves and Biz Botryl, the album is famously laden with intricate secrets, which sparked numerous fan theories and urban legends upon its release, including a rumored halt in production. Notably, the CD and vinyl versions featured different track listings, with the band confirming the vinyl order was a technical compromise due to space limitations and expressing a preference for the CD's sequence. The initial US release contained typographical and spelling errors in the booklet and lyrics, which are now prized collector's items. The album's central themes explore meditation, the astral projection of mind and body, and the concept of dualism, while also weaving in personal narratives such as loss and life stages. Musically, Lateralus is characterized by astonishing rhythmic complexity, frequently featuring instruments playing in different, unsynchronized time signatures and continuous meter changes, a demanding technique the band meticulously developed over years. Although its initial critical reception was not as enthusiastic as Ænima, over time, as its layers and secrets have been uncovered, Lateralus has solidified its place as Tool's most charismatic and influential album, significantly impacting later artists like Muse. "Es un disco completamente clave dentro de la historia del rock."
